{{Short description|Japanese physical chemist}}

'''Toshiaki Enoki''' ({{langx|ja|榎 敏明}}; born December 4, 1946) is a Japanese physical chemist.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Researcher Finder Science Tokyo STAR search (研究者詳細 {{!}} 東京科学大学 STAR サーチ in Japanese) |url=https://search.star.titech.ac.jp/titech-ss/lang.act?forward=pursuer.act?from=basic&lang=en&&ssToken=0f6575e33ef7efa2274cf90abdf52094&k=nwbNYpBnBs |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=Search STAR-Institute of Science Tokyo}}</ref> After earning his Ph.D. from [[Kyoto University]], he was appointed as a research associate at the [[Institute for Molecular Science]] in 1977.<ref name=":4" /> His early research focused on the electronic and magnetic properties of [[Organic conductor|organic conductors]] <ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Enoki |first1=Toshiaki |last2=Miyazaki |first2=Akira |date=2004-11-01 |title=Magnetic TTF-Based Charge-Transfer Complexes |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/cr0306438 |journal=Chemical Reviews |volume=104 |issue=11 |pages=5449–5478 |doi=10.1021/cr0306438 |pmid=15535656 |issn=0009-2665|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Graphite intercalation compound|graphite intercalation compounds]] <ref>{{Cite book |last=Enoki |first=Toshiaki |title=Graphite Intercalation Compounds and Applications |date=10 April 2003 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780197561409|url=https://academic.oup.com/book/40728}}</ref>, with particular emphasis on hydrogen adsorption into graphitic galleries.<ref name=":4" /> In 1987, he joined the [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]] (now the [[Institute of Science Tokyo]]) as an associate professor and was promoted to full professor in 1991.<ref name=":0" /> During this period, his research interests shifted toward [[graphene]] - a single atomic layer of graphite and related carbon-based materials, particularly nanosized graphene, or [[nanographene]]. Enoki’s primary focus became the unique geometrical dependence of nanographene sheets in determining their electronic and magnetic properties. In 1996, M. Fujita theoretically predicted the existence of a localized nonbonding state - known as an [[Edge states|edge state]] at the carbon atoms along the zigzag edges of a graphene sheet.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fujita |first1=Mitsutaka |last2=Wakabayashi |first2=Katsunori |last3=Nakada |first3=Kyoko |last4=Kusakabe |first4=Koichi |date=1996-07-15 |title=Peculiar Localized State at Zigzag Graphite Edge |url=https://journals.jps.jp/doi/10.1143/JPSJ.65.1920 |journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan |volume=65 |issue=7 |pages=1920–1923 |doi=10.1143/JPSJ.65.1920 |bibcode=1996JPSJ...65.1920F |issn=0031-9015|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Enoki later confirmed the presence of this edge state experimentally using [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscopy]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kobayashi |first1=Yousuke |last2=Fukui |first2=Ken-ichi |last3=Enoki |first3=Toshiaki |last4=Kusakabe |first4=Koichi |last5=Kaburagi |first5=Yutaka |date=2005-05-25 |title=Observation of zigzag and armchair edges of graphite using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.71.193406 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=71 |issue=19 |article-number=193406 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.71.193406 |arxiv=cond-mat/0503472 |bibcode=2005PhRvB..71s3406K |issn=1098-0121}}</ref> He has contributed to understanding of the electronic, magnetic, and chemical properties of nanographene and related carbon-based materials.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Dresselhaus |first1=Mildred S. |last2=Araujo |first2=Paulo T. |date=2010-11-23 |title=Perspectives on the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for Graphene |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/nn1029789 |journal=ACS Nano |volume=4 |issue=11 |pages=6297–6302 |doi=10.1021/nn1029789 |pmid=21090813 |bibcode=2010ACSNa...4.6297D |issn=1936-0851|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fujii |first1=Shintaro |last2=Enoki |first2=Toshiaki |date=2013-10-15 |title=Nanographene and Graphene Edges: Electronic Structure and Nanofabrication |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ar300120y |journal=Accounts of Chemical Research |volume=46 |issue=10 |pages=2202–2210 |doi=10.1021/ar300120y |pmid=24383129 |issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics and Chemistry of Graphene (Second Edition) |url=https://www.jennystanford.com/9789814800389/physics-and-chemistry-of-graphene-second-edition/ |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=Jenny Stanford Publishing |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Academic career'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=ENOKI Toshiaki |url=https://nrid.nii.ac.jp/nrid/1000010113424/ |access-date=2026-07-19 |website=KAKEN}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

* 1969: BS, [[Kyoto University]]
* 1974: PhD, Kyoto University
* 1977: Research Associate, [[Institute for Molecular Science]]
* 1984: Visiting Scientist, Massachusetts Institute of Technology<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Enoki |first=Toshiaki |date=2018-03-20 |title=From Graphite Intercalation Compounds to Nanographene: Many Years of Collaboration |url=https://millie.pubpub.org/pub/ftvewqn4/release/1 |journal=Celebrating Millie |language=en}}</ref>
* 1987: Associate Professor, [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]]
* 1991: Professor, Tokyo Institute of Technology
* 2000, 2002 - 2004：Visiting Professor, Universite de Rennes I<ref>{{Cite web |title=NANOCON 2016 |url=https://nanocon2016.tanger.cz/cz/profile/214p-prof-toshiaki-enoki-ph-d/ |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=nanocon2016.tanger.cz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3291-5582 |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=orcid.org}}</ref>
* 2003-2004: Visiting Professor, Institute for Molecular Science<ref>{{Cite web |title=Organization and staff of the Institute for Molecular Science, Annual Review 2004, the Institute for Molecular Science |url=https://www.ims.ac.jp/en/about/publication/ann_rev_2004/ar200402.pdf |access-date=2026-08-03|website=the Institute for Molecular Science, Japan}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Annual Review in 2003, Institute for Molecular Science |url=https://www.ims.ac.jp/en/about/publication/ann_rev_2003/ar2003.pdf |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=Institute of Molecular Science, Japan}}</ref>
* 2010-2013: Honorary Professor, Durham University<ref>{{Cite web |title=Researchmap:Toshiaki Enoki |url=https://researchmap.jp/ToshiakiEnoki?lang=en |access-date=2026-08-24}}</ref>
* 2012 : Professor Emeritus, [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]]
* 2012-2022: Program Officer, [[Japan Science and Technology Agency]]
* 2016-2018: Visiting Fellow, Toyota Physical and Chemical Research Institute<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research fellow - Research,  Toyota Physical and Chemical Research Institute　研究｜公益財団法人 豊田理化学研究所 |url=https://www.toyotariken.jp/about/service/research/ |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=公益財団法人 豊田理化学研究所 (Toyota Physical and Chemical Research Institute) |language=ja}}</ref>

* 2011: [[The Chemical Society of Japan]] Award "Edge state of Nanographene and its Electronic and Magnetic Properties"<ref>{{Cite web |title=Edge state of Nanographene and its Electronic and Magnetic Properties |url=http://www.chemistry.or.jp/en/awards/2016/edge-state-of-nanographene-and-its-electronic-and-magnetic-properties.html |access-date=2026-07-19 |website=The Chemical Society of Japan |language=en}}</ref>

Ioffe Institute of Physics |url=https://www.ioffe.ru/ru/institut/istoriya/pochetnye-chleny/?csrfmiddlewaretoken=Ub67bFeGjCYeOFiTK0t2PBNb7uNTOo761kBfQcLPFwDhjQBtypm2TvJKbEEI6Z90&name=%D0%95%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%BA%D0%B8 |access-date=2026-07-19 |website=www.ioffe.ru}}</ref>
* 2015: Prof. C. N. R. Rao Award Lecture, Chemical Research Society of India<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. C.N.R. Rao Award Lecture – Chemical Research Society of India |url=https://crsi-india.org/prof-c-n-r-rao-award-lecture/ |access-date=2026-07-19 |language=en}}</ref>
